$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json,
trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. Precedent for a per-repo port: kubelab,
hive, web and ts-bridge each carry their own copy; the SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`. Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND when the question cannot be
computed, precisely so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear one. But a check
that reports the same thing every time it runs stops being read, which is how a gate degrades
into noise. Ported 2026-09-06 with the ts-bridge port as the template.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over the ten most recent
non-dependabot PRs (#47, #50, #51, #52, #63, #64, #65, #66, #67, #71), reading the issue
comments CodeRabbit posted on each. What it actually emits in this repo, by PR:
## Walkthrough                         -> #47 #64 #71            (a review ran; the attesting marker)
No actionable comments were generated  -> #64 only               (1 of the 3 reviews; too rare to attest on)
## Review limit reached                -> #50 #51 #52 #63 #65 #66 #67  (posted as a `> [!WARNING]` blockquote,
and every one also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai')
## Review skipped                      -> none observed
(no CodeRabbit output)                 -> dependabot PRs (#48 #49 #68 #69 #79 #80 #81)
Seven of ten PRs drew a quota decline, which is why the vendor entry below is advisory and
why the github-actions entry exists.
The `github-actions` entry declares an actor that is about to exist rather than one that was
observed: .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml lands in the same PR as this file. Read the entry's
own `why` for what has and has not been verified, and treat the first run of pr-agent.yml as
the check that makes it real.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change, and in this repo it is the normal case rather than the exception -- measured over the ten PRs listed in $comment, seven drew 'Review limit reached', so a decline that REFUSED would make the gate red more often than green and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. 'No actionable comments were generated' is deliberately NOT a review marker: it appeared on one of the three reviews here (#64) and always alongside '## Walkthrough', so it adds no attestation and would be a second string to keep true.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here — kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot] and dotfiles has 172. It has NEVER been observed in pollex, because this workflow has not run here, and it cannot run until the NAN_API_KEY secret is set (`dotf secrets sync ci --repo mlorentedev/pollex`): the first green run of pr-agent on a pollex PR is the verification, and until then this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #66 (chore(master): release 1.8.3): exactly these three paths. The third is release-please-config.json's `extra-files` jsonpath bump of the extension version, so it is part of the mechanical signature here and not in the sibling ports. Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch — release-please runs under RELEASE_TOKEN, a human PAT (lesson-069), so an author rule would not fire, and a branch rule would let any branch named to match walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
